Alabama Secretary of State FCPA contributions to Etowah County's candidates since 2023
EFF Atlas of Surveillance (police surveillance technology, searched by department)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2022, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by county and city boards of education, which the Census counts as separate school systems, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts itemized cash contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to county commission, sheriff, revenue commissioner, tax assessor and collector, coroner and constable candidates, filed with the Secretary of State since 2023. Alabama allows business and union contributions. Individuals, in-kind gifts, and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Alabama yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.detail: The Etowah County Sheriff's Office operates 10 Flock Safety automated license plate readers as of September 2025.

Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($3,500,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts itemized cash contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to candidates for mayor and city council, filed with the Secretary of State since 2023. Municipal candidates are placed by the city of their mailing address, which can differ from the town they ran in. Alabama allows business and union contributions. Individuals, in-kind gifts, and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
